item.title: 11 Days, 64 AIs, 530K Lines of Code: A Complete Engineering Retrospective on Rewriting Bun from Zig to Rust
item.description: Jarred Sumner used Claude Fable 5 and 50 dynamic workflows to rewrite 535,496 lines of Zig into Rust in 11 days. An agent pipeline of 1 implementer + 2 adversarial reviewers, peaking at 1,300 lines of code per minute. This isn't 'AI helping you write code' — this is 'AI helping you make decisions.'

item.title: Stop Teaching AI to Code Step by Step: The Claude Code Team's #1 Advice Is 'Give It Back Its Judgment'
item.description: The counterintuitive advice from the Claude Code team at AIE 2026: don't tell Fable when to write tests — let it decide for itself. Likewise, let Fable decide which tasks should be delegated to cheaper models. This strategy is not only cheaper, but more effective.

item.title: Newer Claude Models Are Worse at Using Your Tools: An Engineering Trap of RL Training Backfire
item.description: Armin discovered that Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 are actually more error-prone than older models when calling Pi's custom editing tool — because RL training overfits them to Claude Code's built-in tools. This is a wake-up call for every third-party coding harness.

item.title: SOTA on Paper, Engineering Traps in Production: Claude Opus 5's Hidden Risks
item.description: Claude Opus 5 tops Frontier-Bench and CursorBench at half the price of Fable 5. We look past the benchmarks to three engineering traps most teams miss.

item.title: Agent Clusters - When AI Starts 'Forming Squads'
item.description: Deep dive into Claude Code's multi-Agent architecture: three spawning methods - sub-Agents, Fork mode, and Coordinator mode - plus Agent Swarm collaboration and verification Agent mechanisms.

item.title: Hello World Agent: A Complete Minimal Runnable Agent Example
item.description: Build a complete Hello World Agent from scratch, with line-by-line code explanation, running and debugging, common error analysis, helping you build a complete sensory understanding of ADK Go.

item.title: Agent Core Concepts: Model, Tool, Instruction — The Three Pillars
item.description: Deep understanding of Agent's three elements in ADK Go: Model (model), Tool (tools), Instruction (instructions), and how they work together.

item.title: Sub-Agents vs Agent Teams: The Architecture Decision That Can Wreck Your System
item.description: The real question is how to choose between Sub-Agents and Agent Teams. Most people immediately think of multi-agent systems when tasks get complex, but that's often the wrong starting point. Understanding the answer can save you countless hours of rework.

item.title: OpenClaw Multi-Bot Team Collaboration: Three Architecture Patterns Compared
item.description: Build multiple independent Telegram Bots into a collaborative Agent team. This article covers three architecture patterns and complete configuration methods.

item.title: OpenAI Finally Reveals Codex's Core: The Counterintuitive Design That Shocked Me
item.description: Last night, an OpenAI engineer exposed Codex's agent loop completely. Now I understand why they dare to open source it - Claude Code has met its match.

item.title: Agno-Go: Building AI Agents in Go - What's it Like Being 16x Faster than Python?
item.description: Rewriting AI Agent framework in Go brings 16x performance boost, 180ns agent startup, and only 1.2KB memory footprint - this is the extreme experience Agno-Go delivers
